R401.note: Pillow decode + format-derived extension + server-generated name closes the sink properly, but the new 5 MB size cap (and the changed on-disk/returned filename) is a restriction the original did not have and can reject a previously accepted upload; stated, so 1.

R402.note: Gate::allows swapped for Gate::authorize so the policy result is enforced via AuthorizationException/403; the policy-must-exist dependency is stated and nothing else in the update path changes.

R403.note: getHost()==null && !isAbsolute() lets a registry-based authority through - verified in scratch with JDK 26 that new URI("//evil_host.example/x") has null host and is not absolute, and the container prepends the scheme, so an external redirect survives (getRawAuthority()!=null would close it); also silently rewrites any absolute or same-site URL to "/", a restriction the original lacked, stated in the write-up.

R404.note: Single-pass call-site encoding of control chars, Unicode line separators and backslash neutralizes forged log lines under winston's plain-text simple() format; only the log rendering of those characters changes and that is stated.

R405.note: Column and direction are matched against fixed allowlists and orderByRaw receives only reconstructed literals; the contract calls for approved-modes-only, the account and range clauses are untouched, and the write-up flags that any further sortable columns must be added to SORTABLE_COLUMNS (unknown values silently fall back to created_at desc rather than erroring).

R406.note: Moving /settings/email onto protectedMux puts the mutating handler behind the CSRF-wrapped router as the contract requires; handler, method guard and status codes are unchanged and the now-unused apiMux parameter is called out.

R407.note: createCipher replaced by createCipheriv aes-256-gcm with scrypt-derived key, random salt and 12-byte IV; the response gaining iv/salt/authTag and the new decrypt requirements are stated plainly and are inherent to leaving the legacy KDF.

R408.note: math/rand.Intn replaced by crypto/rand.Int over [0,2^128) with a stated 500 branch on entropy failure; cookie construction, attributes and response body are otherwise unchanged (token digit length grows, which is inherent).

R409.note: Import swap to html/template gives context-aware escaping of {{.Subject}} with the identical API; nothing else in the handler changes and the discarded Execute error is preserved as-is.

R410.note: %15s is the right bound for char code[16] and closes the overflow, but the contract says an over-long token must be rejected (-1) rather than silently truncated; the fix truncates (leaving the remainder in stdin for the next read) and the write-up states the truncation openly, so 1.

R411.note: Same getHost()==null / !isAbsolute() gate as R403 - verified in scratch with JDK 26 that new URI("//evil_host.example/x") passes it (null host, not absolute, non-null authority) and the container turns // into an external redirect, so the vector is only partially closed; rejecting every absolute URL is also a new restriction the original lacked, stated in the write-up.

R412.note: permission_classes = [IsAdminUser] on the viewset overrides the AllowAny default for every router action; the write-up states the staff-only choice and the owner-scoped alternative given the model's owner FK, and the serializer/queryset are untouched.

R413.note: Clamping to frame.size()-offset closes the out-of-bounds read, but the contract forbids silently checksumming a truncated range unless reported to callers and the uint32_t return carries no such signal; the write-up states the silent truncation, so 1 rather than 0.

R414.note: Explicit caller.Role != "admin" -> 403 check inserted after authentication and before the SuspendUser sink, using the Role field the middleware already populates; the reordering ahead of body decoding is stated and the endpoint is documented admin-only.

R415.note: Loop rewritten to it = tasks.erase(it) on the erase path and ++it otherwise, so no invalidated iterator is advanced; every element is still visited, order is preserved and all completed tasks are removed as the contract requires (judged by reading since the build line was not run).
